title: High availability and zone-aware architecture
description: Design Azure architectures that survive datacenter failures using Availability Zones, zone-redundant services, and cross-region patterns. Learn how to configure App Service, SQL, and VMs for resilience.

data.text: Azure datacenters are grouped into regions, and each region contains multiple Availability Zones—physically separate locations within a 60-mile radius, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. A zone-aware architecture spreads workloads across zones so that a failure in one zone does not bring down your application.

Inside a zone, Azure maintains fault domains (physical racks with independent power) and update domains (groups that reboot one at a time). When you create a virtual machine scale set or App Service plan with zone redundancy, Azure spreads instances across zones automatically. For stateful services like SQL Database, you can choose zone-redundant high availability.

terms.definition: A physically isolated datacenter location within an Azure region, connected by low-latency fiber.
Deployed across multiple zones within the same region for high availability.
Two regions paired by Azure for replication, with at least 300 miles between them.

data.text: Zone redundancy protects against datacenter failures within a region, but entire regions can experience rare, prolonged outages. For critical workloads, add a cross-region layer using Azure Traffic Manager or Front Door. Geo-redundant storage (GRS) replicates data to a paired region asynchronously, usually within minutes.

data.title: Designing for zone awareness
items: Place stateless application tiers in zone-redundant App Service plans or VMSS.
Use zone-redundant SQL or Cosmos DB for stateful data tiers.
Avoid single-zone dependencies such as a single Redis cache without replication.
Test failover behavior in a non-production environment before relying on it.

data.title: Zones are not regions
data.text: A zone-redundant deployment is highly available, not disaster-proof. If the entire region loses connectivity, zone redundancy does not help. Pair it with a cross-region traffic routing strategy for critical applications.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Availability Zones provide physical isolation within a region.
Zone-redundant services distribute instances across zones automatically.
Cross-region replication adds a second layer of protection against regional outages.
Validate zone placement and failover behavior early, not during an incident.
data.takeaway: Zone awareness is the foundation of Azure high availability; cross-region patterns complete the story.
